 Sam Boughedda Wed, 4 November 2026 at 8:38 am GMT-5 2 min read BLKB 
 DX-Y.NYB 
 Investing.com -- Blackbaud (NASDAQ: BLKB) is seeing rapid growth in use of its AI fundraising agent, with gifts attributed to the tool up 70% from September to October, Investing.com has learned. 
 Still guessing which stocks will beat the market? Our AI portfolio updates monthly and is outperforming the S&P 500 by 118%. See this month's list » 
 The number of donors assigned to the Development Agent rose fivefold from the second quarter to the third, while personalized donor touch points from the agent rose 55% over the past 90 days. The average attributed gift rose 44% from September to October. 
 "That tells us we're seeing growth on both sides of the equation: more organizations putting the agent to work, and stronger results as customers expand how they're using it," Chief Executive Mike Gianoni told Investing.com. 
 He did not disclose how many customers use the agent or the dollar value of donations attributed to it. Blackbaud's website cites more than $300,000 over six months, a figure Gianoni said reflects an earlier stage of the program. He added that results have continued to grow since then. 
 A gift counts as attributed to the agent if it comes from a donor assigned exclusively to the agent rather than to a human fundraiser.

 "Importantly, we don't interpret every attributed gift as a donation directly solicited by the agent," Gianoni highlighted. 
 The Development Agent is sold as an annual subscription "designed to let organizations put the agent to work across their donor portfolios." 
 When asked about the potential revenue contribution of AI products in 2027, Gianoni said Blackbaud is not providing 2027 revenue guidance for its AI products, but that the company is "very confident in the position we're building in domain-specific AI for the social impact sector." 
 On its third-quarter call, it was said that 2026 full-year guidance includes no meaningful revenue contribution from them. 
 Blackbaud, whose software is used by nonprofits, schools and foundations, reported last week that third-quarter revenue rose 4.1% to $292.64 million, above the consensus expectation of $292.59 million. EPS of $1.36 was $0.03 better than the analyst estimate of $1.33.
